title: Bimolecular Homolytic Substitution Catalysis with a Europium Photocatalyst for Single Functional Group Cross-Coupling
abstract: Lanthanide photocatalysis has emerged as a promising alternative to precious-metal systems due to its earth abundance, low toxicity, and unique photophysical properties. However, reported lanthanide-based photocatalysts have primarily focused on the generation of reactive radical species, with limited ability to control product selectivity in bond-forming processes.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

title: Heavier-than-expected electron behavior may explain slower electrical flow in alpha-gallium oxide
abstract: Power electronic devices help control the flow of electricity and convert it into forms needed by different machines, such as electric vehicles, renewable energy systems and industrial equipment. Some electrical energy is lost as heat during this process, reducing efficiency and potentially affecting the device's performance. Semiconductor materials that can withstand high voltages, carry electricity efficiently and release heat effectively would make these devices more efficient and reliable.

title: Sequence-Regulated Adhesion of Poly(diethyl glycolide- alt -β-butyrolactone) Synthesized via Enantiomorphic Site-Assisted Stereospecific Alternating Copolymerization
abstract: Biodegradable polyesters can be promising adhesives for their inherent biodegradability, yet their adhesive performance still requires substantial enhancement to meet practical demands. In this work, the alternating sequence effect on adhesive property was explored in the alternating copolymer of S,S-diethylglycolide (S,S-EG, derived from α-hydroxybutyric acid, i.e., α-ethyl-glycolic acid) and R-β-butyrolactone (R-BBL, derived from β-hydroxybutyric acid).
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

title: Unraveling the Intrinsic Interfacial Chemistry of Fluoroethylene Carbonate on Lithium Metal Anodes via a Solvent-Free Model System
abstract: Fluoroethylene carbonate (FEC) is a widely used film-forming additive for stabilizing lithium metal anodes (LMAs), yet its intrinsic interfacial chemistry remains elusive because its reactions are coupled with those of solvents and Li salts in conventional electrolytes. Herein, a solvent-free, dry-processed poly(ethylene oxide)-based solid polymer electrolyte (PEO@Dry) is developed as a platform to isolate the interfacial reactions of FEC without interference from traditional liquid organic solvents.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society
